issues: No integrity problems: the diff changes only one hyperparameter (SCALAR_LR 0.5 -> 0.02). It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, data, seed lines, prepare.py import or evaluation call.

No bugs that would make the result meaningless. This is a legitimate learning-rate change, though it is a 25x cut, so the per-layer scalars will barely move in 300 s. That probably explains why the result is worse.

The numbers support a reject. The candidate is 1.1069 against the incumbent mean of 1.1037, so it is worse by +0.0032 bpb. The sign of z = -0.497 is consistent with 'worse', but |z| < 1 means it is not even a clear regression with n=1 against n=2.

I could not recompute z independently. The individual incumbent runs and the standard deviation are not given. The reported z implies a pooled sd of about 0.0064, which seems large for this setup but cannot be checked from the numbers here.

description: Reduce SCALAR_LR to 0.02 to lower per-layer scalar parameter learning rate and potentially improve val_bpb.
Extend the linear learning rate warmup period to 20% of the total time budget to improve early training stability.
Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 to lower noise in token embedding updates.
Skip the "Stop Gradient on Max Pool" idea: max pooling over attention heads or tokens does not map to a well-defined, minimal change to this causal attention model.
Abort the gradient checkpointing idea: at the current settings memory is not the bottleneck, and checkpointing would only add recompute time inside a fixed 300 s budget.
Increase weight decay from 0.2 to 0.5 to strengthen regularization on Muon optimizer parameters.
Residual Squeeze: reduce ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48, shrinking model_dim from 512 to 384 (8 layers, 3 heads of dim 128) to test whether a narrower model trains better in the fixed 300 s budget.
Reduce the learning rate for the unembedding layer (lm_head) to 0.0001 to further lower val_bpb by slowing down output layer updates.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff changes only one hyperparameter, MATRIX_LR (Muon), from 0.04 to 0.001. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import or the evaluation call.

No bug makes the result meaningless. A 40x lower Muon learning rate is a valid experiment, it just performs badly: 1.3431 against the incumbent mean of 1.1037, which is +0.2394 bpb (worse). The reject decision fits the numbers.

I can't recompute z exactly because the per-run incumbent values and the noise standard deviation weren't provided. The reported z = -37.061 implies a standard deviation of about 0.00646 (0.2394 / 37.061). That is a plausible size for run-to-run noise. The sign is right if negative means the candidate is worse.
Note for planning: z rests on 1 candidate run and 2 incumbent runs, so the variance estimate is weak. The gap is so large that this doesn't change the decision. Don't spend a replicate run on it.

description: Reduce MATRIX_LR to 0.001 to slow down matrix parameter updates relative to scalars, potentially improving embedding quality.
Add a simple, almost no-op variable and check that DOOM does not exist to implement the tortoise gradient accumulation idea.
Reducing the learning rate for the LM head (unembedding layer) improves the output projection stability, resulting in a lower validation bits per byte.
Replace the training cross-entropy with an MSE loss on the LM-head logits, which I am not running because it would not be a valid implementation of this idea.
Reduce LM head temperature to 0.8 to soften output distributions and potentially lower val_bpb.
The crash came from passing an unsupported `temperature=0.8` keyword to `nn.Linear` in the forward pass, so I removed that argument and left the lm_head call as a plain linear projection.
Try lowering AdamBetas to (0.1, 0.99) to test if reduced momentum smoothing helps val_bpb.

Skip the residual inversion idea: the skip path already has learnable per-layer scales (resid_lambdas, initialized to 1.0), and zero-initialized c_proj layers already make each block start as identity, so a fractional skip scale would duplicate existing mechanisms.
Apply layer-specific learning rates by multiplying head-layer LRs with a cosine decay factor based on depth, which stabilizes early layers while fine-tuning later ones.
